sanskrit: ajo bhāgas tapasas taṃ tapasva taṃ te śocis tapatu taṃ te arciḥ | yās te śivās tanvo jātavedas tābhir vahainaṃ sukṛtām ulokam ||
english: O unborn portion of ascetic heat, blaze upon him; let your flame scorch him, let your fire-ray sear him. O Jātavedas, with those gracious forms of yours, carry him to the world of the well-doers.

sanskrit: yās te śocayo raṃhayo jātavedas tanvaḥ krūrāḥ parīṅkhayante | ajaṃ yantam anu tās te sam ṛṇvatām athetarābhiḥ śivatamābhiḥ śṛtaṃ kṛdhi ||
english: Those swift, fierce forms of yours, O Jātavedas, that rush swirling around — let them gather and follow the goat as it goes; then with those other, most benign forms, render him well-cooked and fit.

sanskrit: ava sṛja punar agne pitṛbhyo yas ta āhutaś carati svadhābhiḥ | āyur vasāna upa yātu śeṣaḥ saṃ gacchatāṃ tanvā suvarcāḥ ||
english: O Agni, release again to the fathers him who, offered into you, moves among the ancestral oblations. Let the remainder come clothed in vitality; may he unite with his body, radiant and glorious.

sanskrit: ati drava sārameyau śvānau caturakṣau śabalau sādhunā pathā | adhā pitṝn suvidatrām̐ upehi yamena ye sadhamādaṃ madanti ||
english: Pass swiftly by the two dogs of Saramā, the four-eyed brindled ones, by the good path. Then approach the fathers who are generous in their gifts, those who rejoice in common festivity with Yama.

sanskrit: yau te śvānau yama rakṣitārau caturakṣau pathirakṣī nṛcakṣasā | tābhyām enaṃ pari dhehi rājan svasti cāsmā anamīvaṃ ca dhehi ||
english: O Yama, your two guardian dogs, the four-eyed watchers of the road, men-beholding — place this man safely in their care, O king, and grant him well-being and freedom from affliction.

sanskrit: urūṇasāv ity ekā ||
english: "With broad nostrils" — thus one verse.

sanskrit: soma ekebhyaḥ pavate ghṛtam eka upāsate | yebhyo madhu prajāvati tāṃś cid evāpi gacchatāt ||
english: Soma is purified for some; others attend upon the clarified butter. May he also go to those for whom honey flows abundantly with offspring.

sanskrit: ye ca pūrva ṛtasācā ṛtajātā ṛtāyavaḥ | pitṝn tapasvato yama tapojām̐ api gacchatāt ||
english: Those of former times who are followers of cosmic order, born of order, seekers of order — O Yama, may he also go to those austere fathers, born of ascetic power.

sanskrit: tapasā ye anādhṛṣyās tapasā ye svar yayuḥ | tapo ye cakrire mahas tāṃś cid evāpi gacchatāt ||
english: Those who are invincible through ascetic heat, those who by ascetic power have gone to the sun — those who have made asceticism their greatness — may he too go to those very ones.

sanskrit: sahasraṇīthāḥ kavayo ye gopāyanti sūryam | ṛṣīn tapasvato yama tapojām̐ api gacchatāt ||
english: Those thousand-pathed seers who guard the sun — O Yama, may he also go to those austere seers, born of ascetic power.

sanskrit: ye yudhyante pradhaneṣu śūrāso ye tanūtyajaḥ | ye vā sahasradakṣiṇās taṃś cid evāpi gacchatāt ||
english: Heroes who fight in the thick of battle, those who give up their bodies — or those who give gifts of a thousand — may he also go to those very ones.

sanskrit: syonāsmai pṛthivī bhava- -anṛkṣarā niveśinī | yacchāsmai śarma saprathāḥ ||
english: O Earth, be gentle and soft for him, thornless, a resting place. Grant him wide and sheltering refuge.

sanskrit: asaṃbādhe pṛthivyā urau loke mahīyate | svadhā yāś cakṛṣe jīvaṃ tās te santu madhuścutaḥ ||
english: In the broad, unconfined expanse of Earth he shall be honored. The ancestral offerings that you drew upon while living — may those flow sweet as honey for you.

sanskrit: hvayāmi te namasā ma imaṃ gṛham upa jujuṣāṇa ehi | saṃ gacchasva pitṛbhir yac ca dattaṃ syonās tvā vātā upa vāntu śagmāḥ ||
english: I call you with reverence — come to this my house, delighting in it. Meet with the fathers and with what has been given; may kindly and gentle winds breathe upon you.

sanskrit: ā tvā vahantu maruta udavāhā udaplutaḥ | ajena kṛṇvantaḥ śītaṃ varṣeṇo yantu bāl iti ||
english: May the Maruts carry you, the storm-gods that bear up the waters, the flood-lifted ones. Making coolness with the rain-goat, may they go — so be it!

sanskrit: ud ahvam āyur āyuṣe kratve dakṣāya jīvase | svāṅ gacchatu te mano adhā pitṝn api drava ||
english: I have called up life-force for life, for resolve, for vitality, for living. Let your mind go to its proper place; and then run to the fathers.

sanskrit: mā te mano māsur aṅgānāṃ mā ramaś ca te | mā te hāsta tanvaḥ kiṃ caneha ||
english: May your mind not remain here, nor the marrow of your limbs, nor your delight. May nothing of your body linger here.

sanskrit: mā vṛkṣaḥ saṃ bādhiṣṭa mā devī pṛthivī mahī | lokaṃ pitṛṣu vittvā- -edhasva yamarājasu ||
english: May no tree press you down; may the great divine Earth not oppress you. Having found your place among the fathers, prosper in the realm of King Yama.

sanskrit: yat te aṅgaṃ vinihitaṃ parācair apānaḥ prāṇo ya u te paretaḥ | yat te saṃgatya pitaraḥ sanīḍā ghāse ghāsam ā sādayantu ||
english: The limb of yours that was turned away from here, the outbreath and the inbreath that have departed from you — having gathered together, may the fathers who share the same nest settle you bite by bite into your food.

sanskrit: apemaṃ jīvā arudhan gṛhebhyas taṃ nir ūhata pari grāmād itaḥ | mṛtyo yamasyāsi dūtaḥ pracetā asūn pitṛbhyo gamayāṃ cakartha ||
english: The living have driven him away from the houses; carry him out and away from this village. O Death, you are Yama's wise messenger; you have dispatched the life-breaths to the fathers.

sanskrit: ye dasyavaḥ pitṛṣu praviṣṭā jñātimukhā ahutādaś caranti | parāpuro nipuro ye caranti tān asmād yajñāt pra dhamantu devāḥ ||
english: Those demons who have entered among the fathers, who go about bearing the faces of kinsmen and devouring the unoffered portions — those who roam about as wreckers and destroyers — may the gods drive them away from this sacrifice.

sanskrit: saṃ viśantv iha pitaraḥ svā naḥ syonaṃ kṛṇvantu pratiranta āyuḥ | tebhyaḥ śakema haviṣā yakṣamāṇā jyog jīvantaḥ śaradaḥ purūcīḥ ||
english: May our own fathers come together here, make things gentle for us, and extend life. May we be able to worship them with offerings, living long, through many autumns.

sanskrit: yāṃ te dhenuṃ nigṛṇāmi yaṃ vā te kṣīra odanam | tenā janasyāsau bhartā yo 'trāsad ajīvanaḥ ||
english: The cow I declare for you, or the rice-and-milk offering I name for you — by that let that person there be sustained, the one who was here and without livelihood.

sanskrit: aśvāvatīṃ pra tara yā suśevā ṛkṣīkāṃ vā prataraṃ navīyaḥ | yas tvā jaghāna vadhyaḥ so astu mā so anyad vidata bhāgadheyam ||
english: Cross over by the horse-adorned path, that pleasant one, or proceed further by the path of the Ṛkṣas, newer still. Whoever slew you — let him be the one deserving to be slain; may he find no other share or fortune.

sanskrit: yamaḥ parastād avaro vivasvān tataḥ paro nāti paśyāmy anyat | yame adhvaro adhi me niviṣṭo bhuve vivasvān anvātatāna ||
english: Yama is beyond, Vivasvān is below him; beyond that I see nothing else. The sacrifice was established for me upon Yama; Vivasvān stretched it out over the earth.

sanskrit: apāgūhann amṛtāṃ martyebhyaḥ kṛtvī suparṇām adadhur vivasvate | utāśvināv abharad yat tad āsīd ajahād u dvā mithunā saraṇyūḥ ||
english: They hid the immortal woman from mortals; having shaped her as a fair-winged one, they gave her to Vivasvān. What was then born, the Aśvins carried away; Saraṇyū abandoned two twin pairs.

sanskrit: ye nikhātā ye paroptā ye dagdhā ye coddhitāḥ | sarvāṃs tān agna ā vaha pitṝn haviṣe attave ||
english: Those who are buried, those who are scattered in the ground, those who are cremated, those who are exposed — O Agni, bring them all, the fathers, to eat the oblation.

sanskrit: ye ceha pitaro ye ceha na yāṃś ca vidma yām̐ u ca na pravidma | tvaṃ vettha yadi te jātavedaḥ svadhābhir yajñaṃ sukṛtaṃ juṣantām ||
english: The fathers who are here and those who are not here, those whom we know and those whom we do not know — you know them, O Jātavedas; may they enjoy this well-performed sacrifice with the ancestral offerings.

sanskrit: śaṃ tapa māti tapo agne mā tanvaṃ tapaḥ | vaneṣu śuṣmo astu te pṛthivyām astu yad dharaḥ ||
english: Blaze with blessing, O Agni; do not scorch overmuch; do not scorch the body. Let your fierce vigor be in the forests; let your golden heat be in the earth.

sanskrit: dadāmy asmā avasānam etad ya eṣa āgan mama ced abhūd iha | yamaś cikitvān praty etad āha mamaiṣa rāya upa tiṣṭhatām iha ||
english: I grant him this resting place — this one who has come here and is now mine. Yama, the wise one, answered thus: "Let this one abide here in my wealth."
